objective: Test whether local-model evidence selection adds value over a competent adaptive rule policy in public-data anomaly verification.

cost_model.field_cost_note: No physical measurements are collected. Costs for real field acquisition are unknown and not inferred from query counts.

full_information: All four actions cost four units. Only budget-four comparisons are like-for-like; no free full-information baseline at lower budgets.
label_separation: Anonymous case identifiers; original fault filenames and severity are unavailable to strategies.

data_tracks.bdg2: Measured historical replay without equipment fault truth; no fault accuracy claimed.
data_tracks.lbnl: Single-system simulated fault/normal cases with isolated labels; not real building deployment.
data_tracks.perturbation: Explicit post-hoc record corruption with separate provenance; not a simulated physical sensor intervention.

numerics: A shared deterministic feature and diagnosis engine supplies every number. The local model only selects a next allowed action.
freeze_gate: Final protocol, code hashes, development calibration and case IDs must be frozen before holdout evaluation. Failures are retained; changes after opening holdout invalidate pristine-holdout claims.
decision_rule: Retain an innovation claim only if improvement over adaptive rules is demonstrated at comparable information and cost. Otherwise narrow to a reproducible verification workbench and describe LLM selection as optional.
